subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
skillName: Patterns of Motion Predict Future Motion

items.prompt:
Many objects, like swings, move in
A) repeating patterns
B) no pattern ever
C) only one direction forever
D) random jumps only

steps: Swings and pendulums move in repeating patterns.

items.prompt:
A pattern of motion can be used to
A) predict future motion
B) stop time
C) change colors
D) nothing

steps: Repeating patterns let us predict what happens next.

items.prompt:
A ball rolls the same path three times. The fourth roll will likely take
A) a new random path
B) the same path
C) no path
D) a straight line up

steps: The repeating pattern means the fourth roll matches.

items.prompt:
Why can a repeating pattern predict future motion?
A) Because it repeats the same way
B) Because it is random
C) Because it never happens again
D) It cannot
items.answer: A) Because it repeats the same way

steps: A repeating pattern keeps happening the same way.

items.prompt:
A pendulum swings 10 times in 20 seconds. In 40 seconds it will swing about
A) 5 times
B) 10 times
C) 20 times
D) 100 times

steps: Twice the time gives about twice the swings.

items.prompt:
A toy train loops in 15 seconds each time. After 30 seconds it is
A) halfway
B) back at the start after two loops
C) off the track
D) stopped forever
items.answer: B) back at the start after two loops

steps: Two loops in 30 seconds return it to the start.

items.prompt:
A merry-go-round turns once every 10 seconds. In 1 minute it turns about
A) 2 times
B) 6 times
C) 10 times
D) 60 times

steps: 60 seconds divided by 10 seconds per turn equals 6 turns.

items.prompt:
Which is HARDER to predict?
A) A swing with a steady back-and-forth
B) A single random movement with no pattern
C) A clock's steady hands
D) A looping train
items.answer: B) A single random movement with no pattern

steps: Without a repeating pattern there is nothing to predict from.
